findings.title: A late success after a human :failed resolution replays as a FAILED outcome with a nil error (carried forward from CF04-REL-01)
findings.recommendation: In EffectDispatcher#resolve_decision make the :failed branch read the current head attempt and return its error and identity; keep the succeeded-attempt lookup for :return. Add one regression driving expiry -> attempt 2 repairable failure -> late attempt 1 success -> operator :failed resolution.
findings.narrowing: Not reachable on the in-memory Runtime::EffectsJournal, which refuses a non-owner attempt token (/tmp/f17_probe_late.rb). Durable-journal-only.

findings.title: EpisodeNodes::RISK_RANK is a Ruby-literal risk-class table, duplicating IntentCatalog::RISK_CLASSES with no shared definition
findings.recommendation: Derive the ordering from IntentCatalog's ordered RISK_CLASSES instead of a second literal; if the coordinator rules the wire enum exempt from B9, keep the table but assert it equals IntentCatalog::RISK_CLASSES. No new class.
findings.qualifier: Fail-closed: fetch(risk_class, 99) ranks an unknown class above every ceiling, so no unsafe action was proven. Major, not critical.

findings.title: The approval records a plan_digest that is never compared against the plan it approves; the replay path reuses approvals by plan_id/step_id only
findings.recommendation: In SessionSteps#journaled_verdict require the matched approval's plan_digest to equal accepted.fetch('plan_digest') before returning its stored verdict, raising the existing typed error on mismatch.
findings.note: The patch half IS bound three ways (arguments_digest, preview_digest, expected_sha256 re-verified against the live workspace). Only the plan half is unverified. Exploit path unproven.

findings.title: Tamoz::Core::INTENT_WATCH_TYPE is a Ruby-literal domain vocabulary word consumed by the kernel catalog
findings.recommendation: Take the watch type from the catalog's own declaration (an explicit watch_type key in the domain JSON, defaulted by test/support/domain_loader.rb), or record the wire-constant exemption in the B9 note. One change, no new module.
findings.qualifier: gems/tamoz-agent-kernel/lib contains zero intent type names other than through this alias; the catalog itself is clean.

findings.title: The episode path collapses every failed effect into one untyped ProtocolError with no diagnostic
findings.recommendation: At enforce_successful_outcome! raise a class reflecting the outcome (EffectUnknownError/ModelCallError for the model subject, the existing ToolError family for the tool subject) carrying result.outcome.error, instead of collapsing both into ProtocolError.
findings.note: Local blur only: the taxonomy elsewhere is boundary-correct and error identity survives replay (code defaults to "replayed" at errors.rb:52-54).

findings.title: CF04-REL-01 is durable-journal-only; the in-memory Runtime journal refuses a non-owner attempt token
findings.recommendation: None. Recorded so the coordinator does not widen CF04-REL-01's blast radius.
findings.probe: /tmp/f17_probe_late.rb -> late success REJECTED: Tamoz::CheckpointConflictError: effect attempt token is stale or does not own current attempt

findings.title: Every non-deterministic and external call site across gems/*/lib routes through EffectDispatcher.run; no FX violation found
findings.recommendation: None. The two raw HTTP clients in this gem (EpisodeModelTransport, WitnessGateway) are the dispatcher's own perform block and the server-side signing gateway respectively, not bypasses.
